## ★ The verification target (b) — V8's onset-level representation, CONFIRMED

`reading_pass/population.md` V8, line 109, cites this paper's **title + §1** for *"a recent
graph-based system replaces frame quantisation with one representation per onset and reports it as
the fix"*, quoting three things. All three verify:

- *"Onset-wise Predictions from Note-wise Features"* — the printed subtitle, page 1. **Verbatim.**
- fixed frames *"unnatural for scores… capturing varying amounts of musically relevant context"* —
  §1, page 1: *"However, such a representation is unnatural for scores and has the added practical
  disadvantage of being time-limited (for example regarding notes extending beyond the current
  window) and, due to the fixed-length (in terms of score time) constraint, capturing varying
  amounts of musically relevant context."* **Verbatim, the record's ellipsis compressing the
  time-limited clause.**
- edge-contraction pooling *"yields the learned representation at the onset level"* — §1, page 1:
  *"an edge contraction pooling layer that combines convolution at the note level but yields the
  learned representation at the onset level."* **Verbatim.**

§3.2, page 3, states the same as the design: *"Our approach to automatic Roman Numeral analysis no
longer treats the score as a sequence of quantized time frames but rather as a graph."* §2, page 2,
gives the authors' reason: *"Should a musicologist perform music analysis on a piece of music, they
would consider the individual notes existing in the score. Thus, a time frame representation would
come across as unnatural for symbolic music and in particular for such an analysis task."*
**Nothing is owed to V8.**

**ONE PRECISION, for the L1 charter rather than for V8.** The representation is **onset-wise
only**. The graph's nodes are notes and its edge types are *onset* (notes starting together),
*during* (one starting while another sounds), *follow* (one starting when another ends) and
*silence* (§3.2, page 3); the pooling contracts along the ONSET edges, so the sequence handed to
the recurrent part has one element per onset (§3.3, equations 2–3, page 4). **Offsets enter as edge
relations and not as partition points.** The record's L1 partition-point ground — Pardo and
Birmingham, whose partition points are the note onsets **and offsets** — is therefore a different
grid from this one, not the same one. Routed to the L1 and L2 detail specifications beside V8;
**V8's own wording, "one representation per onset", is exactly right and nothing is owed to it.**

**Printed title, page 1:** *"ROMAN NUMERAL ANALYSIS WITH GRAPH NEURAL NETWORKS: ONSET-WISE
PREDICTIONS FROM NOTE-WISE FEATURES"*. **Authors:** Emmanouil Karystinaios¹ and Gerhard Widmer^(1,2)
— ¹ Institute of Computational Perception, Johannes Kepler University Linz, Austria; ² LIT AI Lab,
Linz Institute of Technology, Austria. **The arXiv stamp down the left margin of page 1:**
*"arXiv:2307.03544v2 [cs.SD] 12 Jul 2023"*. **The attribution box at the foot of page 1:** *"© E.
Karystinaios and G. Widmer. Licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License
(CC BY 4.0). **Attribution:** E. Karystinaios and G. Widmer, 'Roman Numeral Analysis with Graph
Neural Networks: Onset-wise Predictions from Note-wise Features', in Proc. of the 24th Int. Society
for Music Information Retrieval Conf., Milan, Italy, 2023."*

**The bibliography's row** (`docs/research_papers/BIBLIOGRAPHY.md` **line 68**) reads in full:

venue, the year and the URL to match on. **What the record does name is right:** `population.md` V8

**(b) THE ROW'S TITLE IS THE MODEL'S NAME, NOT THE PAPER'S.** *ChordGNN* is not the printed title,

## What an L2 detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

- **★ MUST ARGUE AGAINST — the multi-head architecture, which is DP-A's rival for the third row of
  group 3 running.** Eleven heads on one shared encoder, decided in one pass with no consistency
  enforced, and the machinery that undoes the separation applied **after training** over the heads'
  logits. The progress record's summaries of the two earlier reads, read whole this session, record
  row 45's system as six such heads and row 48's as eleven with a re-fused *reconstruction*; this
  one has eleven with a re-deciding *pass*, read here at its own object. **What a detail
  specification must meet is that all three undo the separation downstream of the deciding**, which
  is where DP-A's own cut is. Routed to L2's detail specification and to the findings surface's DP-A
  block.
- **★ A MEASURED ARGUMENT FOR DP-A's CHOSEN "NO" THAT THE RECORD DOES NOT CARRY, STATED BY AUTHORS
  INSIDE THE RIVAL LINEAGE.** §5.1's sentence, quoted in full above, plus the BPS block: AugmentedNet
  scores **higher on Key, Degree, Quality and Root** and **lower on the Roman numeral built from
  them**, and the authors read that as their own model obtaining *"more meaningfully interrelated
  predictions"*. **A per-component win that does not become a joint win is DP-A's argument**, and
  here it is measured rather than asserted. Its bound travels with it: the comparison is between two
  different architectures and not an ablation inside one, no uncertainty is printed on any of the
  cells, and the effect on the Roman numeral column of the BPS block is +0.8. Routed to the findings
  surface's DP-A block and to L2's detail specification; **applied nowhere.**
- **★ A PRECISION ON WHAT "UNDOING THE SEPARATION" BUYS, FROM THIS PAPER'S OWN CONFIGURATION
  STUDY.** The paper measures **two different kinds** of cross-head machinery and reports them
  differently. The post-processing — a reconciliation over all heads after training — gains **+2.9**
  Roman numeral points on both test sets. **NADE — the intra-task-dependency mechanism of [8], which
  is the very work V9's parenthesis names** — gains **+2.1** over the baseline but is **−0.7**
  against the dynamically weighted loss, and §6 concludes that *"techniques for carrying prediction
  information across tasks are not particularly beneficial or necessary for such a model."* **The
  conclusion's sentence is stronger than the table read on its own**, NADE beating the baseline; both
  are recorded. **So "machinery to undo the separation" is not one thing**, and a detail
  specification citing DP-A's lineage sentence should say which kind it means. Routed to the
  findings surface's DP-A block.
- **ADAPT — the graph score representation with edge-contraction pooling to the onset level.** This
  is V8's own item and it is L1's territory. **With the precision recorded above: the grid is onsets
  only**, where the L1 charter's partition points are onsets and offsets. Routed to the L1 and L2
  detail specifications.
- **A DATUM ON THE EVALUATION GRID, of a shape the slice has met before.** The model predicts
  onset-wise and the metric is applied on a **fixed 32nd-note grid**, *"in accordance with
  [6,7,9]"*, using **Chord Symbol Recall — a duration-weighted metric**. The paper publishes
  **RN(Onset) beside RN** so the two granularities can be read against each other, and the derived
  differences above are at most 0.6 in either direction. Routed to measurement design beside D-115,
  row 19's mir_eval finding and row 20's WCSR.
- **MUST ARGUE AGAINST — no segmentation decision and no length term at all**, the class rows 45, 47
  and 48 are in. **The sub-shape here is the opposite of row 48's:** the harmonic-rhythm head exists
  AND its logits are consumed by the reconciliation pass, so this system carries a boundary-bearing
  signal into a later stage without ever deciding a boundary. Routed to L2's detail specification.
- **A DP-C DATUM — over-segmentation, worked at the score by the authors.** §5.4's example predicts
  an eighth-note harmonic rhythm against the annotator's half note, and the authors defend it on the
  ground that the model does not group at a higher level. **`reading_pass/l2_slice_reading_progress.md`'s
  summary of the row 45 read records over-segmentation as that paper's authors' most common error
  class** — cited to the progress record, where it was read this session, because **neither row 45's
  extract nor row 45's paper was opened here**. Routed to the findings surface's DP-C block,
  **unmerged with row 18's finding (3)**.
- **A DP-D DATUM.** The Pitch Class Sets task is present, as in row 48, and there is no chord-tone
  assignment: nothing in the model decides which sounding notes belong to the harmony. Routed to the
  findings surface's DP-D block.
- **A DATUM ON WHERE THIS LINEAGE IS GOING, not a finding.** §6 names cadence detection and phrase
  boundary detection as tasks to add — which is the direction candidacy row 52 (AnalysisGNN) takes,
  and which row 52's own reading will meet. Recorded, carried nowhere.

## ★ The verification target (a) — the ratified FIGURE, CONFIRMED at the primary, with four precisions

The record states the item in three places:

- **`FRAMEWORK.md` DP-A, line 681 (the LIVE ground):** *"…conditioning the degree head on the
  tonality, raising degree accuracy from .762 to .859. [FACT — every figure reported by the paper
  named.]"* — **the paper, the system and the author are all unnamed here.**
- **`FRAMEWORK.md` §S4(a), lines 1566–1567 (the sealed first-stage text):** *"RNBert conditions the
  degree head on the tonality and measures degree accuracy rising from .762 to .859."*
- **`reading_pass/population.md` V9, line 110:** *".762→.859 = RNBERT (Sailor 2024), Table 4 lines 4
  vs 6 + §4.1 (degree .762 unconditioned → .859 key-conditioned with teacher forcing; with PREDICTED
  key it is .749 — the teacher-forcing bound travels with the figure)"*.

**EVERY PART OF V9's LOCATOR IS EXACT AT THE OBJECT.** Table 4, page 6, *All data* block:

- **line 4, RNBert (unconditioned): Degree .762**
- **line 6, RNBert (key conditioned, teacher forcing): Degree .859**
- **line 5, RNBert (key conditioned): Degree .749**

The table, the two lines the pair comes from, the third line the bound comes from, and the
conditions attached to each are all as V9 states them. **V9's VERIFIED verdict does not move and no
value changes.** The whole of Table 4 is transcribed in "The measured results" below, so the three
cells can be read in their context.

**THE MECHANISM CONFIRMED.** §3.6 "Key conditioning", pages 4–5, in the paper's own words: *"In
these key-conditioned experiments, we embed the key tokens with a two-layer MLP with hidden and
output dimensions of 256 and GELU activation. We then concatenate this key embedding with the
output from MusicBERT to obtain the input to the Roman numeral classification heads."* And: *"In
training, we employ teacher forcing, that is, we condition on the ground-truth key annotations from
the labeled data. In evaluation, we first predict the key with a separately fine-tuned model, then
condition the chord predictions on these predicted keys."*

**PRECISION (1) — THE PAPER CALLS LINE 6 A SANITY CHECK, NOT A RESULT.** §4.1, page 5, first
paragraph, verbatim:

> *"In Table 4, line 6, it can be seen that conditioning the Roman numeral prediction on the
> ground-truth key (i.e., teacher forcing) has a large effect on degree accuracy. This constitutes a
> sanity check that the conditioning works as expected: if the model knows the key of the
> annotation, its ability to predict the Roman numeral's degree shoots up."*

So the author's own reading of the 9.7-point rise is that the wiring is connected — the model given
the answer to the key does better at the question that depends on it — and not that the machinery
improves the analysis.

**PRECISION (2) — THE DEPLOYABLE CONDITIONING MOVES DEGREE ACCURACY THE OTHER WAY, AND THE AUTHOR
SAYS SO.** Line 5 is the same conditioning with the key **predicted** by a separately fine-tuned
model, which is what a running system would have. Derived at Table 4, sign convention *line 5 minus
line 4, positive meaning the conditioned model higher*: **Degree −.013** (.749 against .762),
Quality −.003, Inversion 0.000, Key +.001, **RN₋root +.004** (.624 against .620). §4.1, page 5–6:

> *"It is somewhat harder to interpret a comparison of RNBert, conditioned on the predicted key
> (line 5), with the unconditonal RNBert (line 4). The unconditional model does better predicting
> degree, but the conditioned model does better predicting the composite RN₋root. These results make
> sense if key conditioning makes the key and Roman numeral predictions more coherent with one
> another."*

*(«unconditonal» is the paper's own spelling at that sentence and is recorded as printed.)* The
author's stated mechanism for the direction is in the same paragraph: an unconditional model that
gets the key wrong will still hit the labelled degree some of the time, which lifts its degree
accuracy without lifting the analysis.

**PRECISION (3) — THE SAME FIGURE IS LOAD-BEARING IN TWO PLACES OF THE RECORD AND THE
TEACHER-FORCING BOUND BEARS ON THEM DIFFERENTLY. This is the reading this extract most wants
carried.** At **§S4's entanglement argument (line 1642)** the claim is that chord and tonality are
entangled, and there the ground-truth key is exactly the right instrument: giving the model the true
tonality and watching the degree accuracy move 9.7 points is a clean demonstration that the degree
decision depends on the tonality, and the bound costs that claim nothing. At **DP-A (line 681) and
§S4(a) (lines 1566–1567)** the same figure is offered as an instance of *"machinery to undo the
separation"* — of a later system's remedy working — and there the bound is the whole of the matter,
because the only measurement of that remedy under conditions a system could actually run in is
**−.013 on the metric the sentence names** and **+.004 on the composite**. **Neither DP-A's live
sentence nor §S4(a)'s carries the bound; V9 does.**

**PRECISION (4) — "THE DEGREE HEAD" IS NARROWER THAN WHAT THE PAPER CONDITIONS.** The key embedding
is concatenated into the input of **all** the Roman numeral classification heads (§3.6), not the
degree head alone. The effect concentrates on degree because, in the author's words at §4.1, *"key
conditioning, with or without teacher forcing, has little effect on the 'quality' and 'inversion'
metrics… since these tasks do not depend on the key: a first-inversion minor chord is a
first-inversion minor chord regardless of the key in which it occurs."* Table 4 bears that out:
Quality −.002 and Inversion 0.000 between lines 4 and 6.

## What an L2 detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

- **★ MUST ARGUE AGAINST — the multi-head architecture, DP-A's rival for the fourth row of group 3
  running**, and here in its narrowest form yet: **four heads**, decided in one pass over a shared
  encoder, with **no consistency enforced anywhere in the model** and the coherence remedy —
  conditioning the Roman numeral heads on the key — **bolted on outside the deciding, trained with
  the true key and run with a predicted one**. The progress record's summaries of the three earlier
  reads, read whole this session, record row 45's system as six heads, row 48's as eleven with a
  re-fused *reconstruction* and row 49's as eleven with a post-hoc *re-deciding pass*; **this one is
  four heads with an *input-side conditioning*.** **What a detail specification must meet is that all
  four undo the separation somewhere other than in the deciding** — which is where DP-A's own cut is
  — **and that this one's remedy is the only one of the four whose deployable measurement is
  reported, and it is negative on the metric the record names.** Routed to L2's detail specification
  and to the findings surface's DP-A block.
- **★ A RIVAL SHAPE FOR WHERE THE REPRESENTATION COMES FROM, NEW TO THIS SLICE.** Every other member
  of group 3 read so far learns its encoder on the analysis task. This one **fine-tunes a
  general-purpose pretrained encoder** and attributes its coherence advantage to *"the robustness of
  the representations MusicBERT learns in its pretraining"* (§4). **That is a claim about where
  analytical competence comes from**, and a detail specification choosing a hand-built factorisation
  over a learned one has to meet it. Its bound: the attribution is the author's stated belief, not a
  measurement — no ablation removes the pretraining. Routed to L2's detail specification and to the
  findings surface's DP-A block.
- **★ MUST ARGUE AGAINST — the input contract runs the opposite way to L0's.** This system **throws
  away the spelling the notated score carries** and argues that the loss is unimportant because the
  spelling can be restored afterwards by a rule (§3.3.1, citing the line of fifths). **The record's
  L0 bullet says spelling is GIVEN and V3 records it measured to help tonality**; row 45's read
  records full spelling measured *not worse while performing a harder task*. **So this paper supplies
  the position DP-F must argue against, stated by an author who chose it for a practical reason —
  the pretrained model's encoding — rather than for an analytical one.** Recorded with the precision
  that the paper offers **no measurement either way**: it does not compare spelled against unspelled
  inputs. Routed to the findings surface's DP-F/G/H block and to L2's and L1's detail specifications
  beside V3 and D-450; **applied nowhere.**
- **★ ADOPT-OR-ARGUE — the salami-slicing grid is the L1 charter's own grid, where row 49's was
  not.** *"at each timestep with one or more onsets or releases"* — **onsets AND releases**, which is
  Pardo and Birmingham's partition-point construction and the L1 charter's ground at V8. **Row 49's
  read recorded that ChordGNN's grid is onsets only; this one is onsets and offsets.** So the two
  neighbouring members of the same lineage sit on opposite sides of the charter's own boundary rule,
  and this one sits on the charter's side. A datum for V8 and for the L1 charter, routed to the L1 and
  L2 detail specifications.
- **★ A TONALITY-AXIS STABILITY MECHANISM WITH ITS COST DECLARED — a fifth worked shape for the
  slice's length-term question.** The slice's four shapes so far are linear/exponential needing no
  segmental decode (rows 19, 20's baseline, 18), Gaussian needing it (row 11's example),
  unbounded-history needing an approximate decode (row 20's chosen model), and no length term at all
  (rows 45, 47, 48, 49). **This paper adds: no length term on the chord axis, and on the TONALITY
  axis a first-order self-transition bonus decoded by Viterbi AFTER the labelling, whose stated
  purpose is to remove key changes of one or two slices and whose stated cost is "a negligible effect
  on the measured accuracy".** It is the same mechanism row 30 fits as a Weber-table transition cost
  and row 26 carries in its transition matrix, **applied here as post-processing rather than inside
  the decision**, and **with no figure published for the negligible-effect claim.** Routed to L2's
  detail specification beside D-347, D-348 and DP-E, and to the findings surface's DP-E block.
- **A DATUM ON THE EVALUATION GRID, of the shape the slice has met before.** The model predicts per
  note, aggregates per salami slice, and the metric is *"the proportion of time that the predicted
  labels are accurate, with 32nd-note resolution"*, following [6] — a **duration-weighted metric on a
  fixed 32nd-note grid**, the same convention row 49's paper uses. Routed to measurement design
  beside D-115, row 19's mir_eval finding and row 20's WCSR.
- **★ AN ON-REPERTOIRE CEILING STATEMENT, from an author of the ground truth we use.** §4.2's
  multiple-acceptable-analyses argument and its *"may place a ceiling on the accuracy of all Roman
  numeral analysis models"*, made about symbolic classical music by a co-author of the When in Rome
  meta-corpus [19]. **Nothing is carried out of it as a value:** it is argued on a priori grounds
  plus qualitative sampling, with no agreement figure and no annotator study. Routed to measurement
  design beside principle #21, D-474, OI-179 and the findings surface's DP-K block; **applied
  nowhere.**
- **A DATUM AGAINST ROW 48's OWN HEADLINE CONTRIBUTION.** §3.4 reports that synthetic training data
  of the kind row 48 introduced and row 49 adopted *"did not… improve the model performance"* here,
  with the author's stated reason. Recorded as a successor's report on a predecessor's mechanism, not
  as a measurement of row 48's system; routed to L2's detail specification.
- **A DATUM ON WHERE THIS LINEAGE IS GOING, not a finding.** §5 names the analysis of dissonant
  idioms — suspensions and passing tones — and melody harmonisation as ready extensions. **That is
  DP-D's question named as a next task by a fourth author group**, and candidacy row 52's own reading
  will meet the same direction. Recorded, carried nowhere.

## ★ The verification target (a) — V9's figure, CONFIRMED at its own cells, with three precisions

**`reading_pass/population.md` V9, line 110:** *".503→.516 = AnalysisGNN Table 4 (w/o logit fusion —
the transformer self-attention layer across every task head's projections — RN(DLC) .503 vs full
.516)"*.

**EVERY PART OF V9's LOCATOR IS EXACT AT THE OBJECT.** Table 4, page 10:

- **w/o Logit Fusion, RN (DLC): .503**
- **full AnalysisGNN, RN (DLC): .516**

The table, the ablated variant, the column and both values are as V9 states them. **V9's VERIFIED
verdict does not move and no value changes.** V9's gloss of the mechanism is also exact: §3.2, page
5, projects each task's raw logits into a common *d*-dimensional space, stacks the projections into
a matrix *P*, and refines them with *"a transformer-style self-attention layer"*, `P̃ = LayerNorm(P +
MultiHeadAttn(P, P, P))`, each task then taking its own row of *P̃* through a fusion head. Whole of
Table 4 is transcribed below.

**PRECISION (1) — THE ABLATION IS NOT UNIFORMLY POSITIVE, AND THE AUTHORS' OWN WORD IS "MODEST".**
Table 4's four columns move as follows for *w/o Logit Fusion* against *full*, sign convention *full
minus ablated, positive meaning the fusion helps*: **RN (DLC) +.013**, **RN (AugNET) +.039**,
**Cadence (DLC) +.017**, **Phrase (DLC) −.010** — and the phrase cell is the one Table 4 prints in
**bold**, the ablated variant being the best phrase score in the table. §5.2, page 10, says so in
terms: *"Removing the logit fusion layer leads to a modest drop in Roman numeral and cadence
performance, indicating that cross-task attention helps reconcile conflicting gradients and share
contextual cues, even though phrase detection can sometimes benefit from more task-specific
signals."* So the record's sentence reports the one column of four on which the machinery gains
least, and the paper itself calls that gain modest and reports one column moving the other way.

**PRECISION (2) — TABLE 4 PRINTS NO UNCERTAINTY OF ANY KIND**, and neither does any other table in
the paper: no spread, no repeat count, no significance test (#24). **The .013 the record's sentence
rests on is a single run**, and it is about an eighth the size of the *w/o Transpositions* decline
in the same column (.516 against .416, a difference of .100), which is the paper's own largest
ablation effect.

**PRECISION (3) — THE .516 IS THE MULTI-CORPUS MODEL, AND THE SAME ARCHITECTURE TRAINED ON THE DLC
ALONE MEASURES HIGHER ON THE SAME TEST SET.** Table 3, page 9: *DLC only* scores **.563** RN on the
DLC where *All corpora (combined)* scores **.516** — derived here, sign convention *combined minus
single-corpus*: **−.047**. So the unified training the logit fusion exists to serve costs about
three and a half times as much RN accuracy on the DLC as the fusion recovers. **Recorded as a
direction, not a result** — no uncertainty is printed on either cell. It is not a correction of
anything the record says; it is what a reader of *"attention across every head's outputs, .503 to
.516"* is not told.

## ★★ The verification target (b) — V1's figures, CONFIRMED at their own cells; and THE CORRECTED STRUCTURAL CLAIM, which is in `FRAMEWORK.md` and NOT in V1

The carried item (b) said the entanglement bullet's pair *"V9 does not locate at all: find where
they are printed."* **They are printed at Table 4, page 10, and `population.md` V1 already locates
them — the fifteenth session had not read V1, which is why the carried item could not say so.**

**`reading_pass/population.md` V1, line 102**, in full: *"Adding a chord-tone head raises the Roman
numeral .506→.516 and cadence .532→.558; authors state structural-note knowledge sharpens harmonic
analysis and conversely"* — **AnalysisGNN (Karystinaios et al., arXiv:2509.06654), Table 4 + §5.2:
w/o auxiliary tasks (the non-chord-tone branch among them) RN(DLC) .506 vs full .516, Cadence(DLC)
.532 vs .558**; quote confirmed.

**AT THE OBJECT, Table 4, page 10:**

- **w/o Aux-Tasks: RN (DLC) .506, Cadence (DLC) .532**
- **full AnalysisGNN: RN (DLC) .516, Cadence (DLC) .558**

**Both values, both columns and both conditions are exactly as V1 states them, and V1's own
parenthetical — *"w/o auxiliary tasks (the non-chord-tone branch among them)"* — is exactly right at
the object.** The quotation is verbatim at §5.2, page 10, the pass having dropped only its opening
*"For example"*: *"For example knowing which notes are structurally relevant sharpens harmonic
analysis, and conversely, learning harmonic context helps the model distinguish chord-tones from
embellishments."* **V1's VERIFIED verdict does not move and nothing is owed to it.**

### ★★ FINDING (1) — THE CORRECTION, AND WHERE IT SITS

**`FRAMEWORK.md` §4.2 line 249 (LIVE, `[FACT]`) and §S5 line 1638 (Appendix B) both say that the
figures come from *"adding a chord-tone head"*. At the object they come from removing ALL the
auxiliary tasks, and the paper isolates no chord-tone head anywhere.**

Three facts establish it, each read at its own page:

- **Table 4's row is labelled `w/o Aux-Tasks`**, not *w/o NCT*, *w/o chord-tone head* or anything
  naming one head. The table has four configurations and none of them removes a single task.
- **§5.2's own sentence is plural and reaches beyond harmony:** *"Removing auxiliary tasks, we
  notice an overall performance drop which indicates that tasks induce positive transfer **among
  them**. **For example** knowing which notes are structurally relevant sharpens harmonic analysis…
  **These cross-task gains go beyond harmonic analysis to structural elements such as cadences,
  phrases and sections.**"* The chord-tone sentence the record quotes is introduced by the paper as
  **one example** of transfer among many tasks.
- **The task set is large and the chord-tone head is one head in it.** §4.3, page 8: the model
  *"predicts 20 distinct properties for each note"* — cadence presence and type, phrase and section
  boundaries, pedal points, metrical strength, harmony onsets/changes, and AugmentedNet's harmonic
  features (local key, tonicization key, root, bass, harmonic rhythm, inversion, quality,
  pitch-class set, common Roman numeral, chord degree), plus new note-level booleans for whether a
  note is the bass, the root, or part of the expected chordal structure. §3.2, page 6 calls the
  Non-Chord-Tone branch *"This auxiliary head"* — one of them.

**THE BOUND, STATED SO THE CORRECTION IS NOT READ WIDER THAN IT IS:** the paper never enumerates
which tasks the `w/o Aux-Tasks` configuration removes. It may mean every task other than the three
Table 4 evaluates, or some smaller set. **What is established either way is that it is not the
chord-tone head alone, because no configuration in the paper removes one head.**

**WHY THIS IS A CORRECTED STRUCTURAL CLAIM AND NOT A PRECISION.** The record does not merely compress
here; it names a different mechanism from the one measured. The difference is load-bearing at the
place the sentence sits: **§4.2's bullet is one of the four legs of the framework's own entanglement
argument, the argument from which the whole decomposition follows** (*"Therefore those four are one
decision"*, line 264), and the leg it supports is *Elaboration ↔ chord*. A measurement of "all
auxiliary tasks together help harmonic analysis" is weaker evidence for that specific coupling than
"a chord-tone head helps harmonic analysis", because the auxiliary set contains cadence, phrase,
section, pedal and metrical-strength heads whose transfer is a different claim. **The figures are
right, the paper is right, and the mechanism the record attributes them to is not the mechanism the
paper ablates.**

### ★★ FINDING (2) — THE SECOND HALF OF THE SAME CORRECTION: "IN BOTH DIRECTIONS" IS MEASURED IN ONE

Four places of the record say the coupling is measured in both directions. At the object **one
direction is measured and the other is stated by the authors with no figure of any kind.**

- **Measured:** removing the auxiliary tasks costs RN and cadence (Table 4). That is
  *chord-tone-and-other-task knowledge → harmonic and structural analysis*.
- **Not measured:** *harmonic context → chord-tone discrimination*. **The paper reports no
  non-chord-tone accuracy, F-measure or error rate anywhere** — Tables 1, 2, 3 and 4 carry no NCT
  column, and no figure for the NCT branch appears in the running text. The claim exists only in
  §5.2's *"and conversely, learning harmonic context helps the model distinguish chord-tones from
  embellishments"*, which is prose.

**§4.2 (line 249) and §S5 (line 1638) are the two careful places**: each opens with *"measures the
coupling in both directions"* but then attributes the second half to *"its authors state that"*, so
a careful reader can separate them. **DP-D (line 708), A.3 (line 1141) and DP4 (line 1812) are
not**: *"the measured benefit running in both directions"*, *"the measured two-way benefit of a
chord-tone head"*, *"the 2025 measurement shows the benefit running in both directions"* — each
asserts a measurement in both directions outright, and **DP-D's is one of the three grounds for a
CHOSEN design point.**

**WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT MOVE.** It moves **no verdict**: DP-D's chosen answer keeps its other two
grounds (the analyst's own note at `003 m4`; ledger C26), and the one measured direction still runs
the way DP-D needs. It moves **no value** — every figure is confirmed. **What it corrects is what the
record may say the paper measured**, at four places, one of which is a chosen design point's live
ground. **This is the same shape as row 45's finding (1)** — there DP-A said *"the papers measure
what happens when they are allowed to disagree"* of a paper that measures nothing about it; here
DP-D says the benefit is measured in both directions of a paper that measures one. **Recorded beside
row 45's finding and merged with it nowhere.**

**GRADED A STOP OF THE REMEDIAL COMMISSION §5 CLASS, WITH THE REASONING STATED SO IT CAN BE
OVERRULED.** A reader may hold that findings (1) and (2) are precisions rather than corrections, on
the ground that every figure is reported by the paper — which is all the `[FACT]` tags claim — and
that the correction, stated accurately, leaves DP-D's chosen answer standing. **This side grades
them a correction and not a precision because the record names a mechanism the paper does not
ablate and a measurement the paper does not report, which is a claim about what the primary
contains rather than a compression of it — the line row 45's and row 50's readings drew between the
two.** The facts for both readings are above. **Nothing is amended.**

## ★ The verification target — §S4(a)'s universal AT ITS STARTING POINT: CONFIRMED, with three precisions

**What was to be verified**, as the progress record's carried item (a) states it: *"does the 2018
paper predict those five as separate heads, and are they those five?"*

**AT THE OBJECT: YES, and they are exactly those five, in the paper's own words and in the record's
own order.**

**Table 1, page 93**, captioned *"Chord function labels in the BPS-FH dataset, including key, primary
degree (pri. deg.), secondary degree (sec. deg.), chord quality, and chord inversion"*, transcribed
cell by cell and re-read at the image:

| Label | Dim | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Key | 24 | 24 major and minor keys |
| Pri. deg. | 21 | 7 Roman numerals by 3 (neutral, ♯, ♭) |
| Sec. deg. | 21 | 7 Roman numerals by 3 (neutral, ♯, ♭) |
| Quality | 10 | M, m, a, d, M7, m7, D7, d7, h7, a6 |
| Inversion | 4 | 0th, 1st, 2nd, 3rd |

**§1, page 90**, in the paper's own words: *"we first build a new dataset comprising five different
chord functions, namely the key, primary degree, secondary degree, quality, and inversion."* **§4,
page 93:** *"The output layer is a 80-D vector containing the classes for the five tasks listed in
Table 1. Each class is one-hot encoding, and the Softmax function is used for the output vector."*
*(Derived here: 24 + 21 + 21 + 10 + 4 = 80, which is the output dimension the paper states — an
arithmetic check of the transcription against the paper's own sentence.)*

**So §S4(a)'s universal is TRUE at its starting point.** Row 47's read established that the same
universal is TRUE of the same authors' 2019 paper and FALSE of their 2021 paper, whose Table 3 gives
two outputs (that is row 47's finding (3), open with the user, **not restated as settled, not merged
with anything here, and not built on**). **This read settles the other end: the system the universal
is named after does predict those five and no others.**

**PRECISION (1) — "SEPARATE HEADS" IS EXACT FOR ONE OF THE PAPER'S TWO ARCHITECTURES AND LOOSE FOR
THE OTHER, AND THE PAPER MEASURES THEM AGAINST EACH OTHER.** Figure 2, page 93, gives two:

- **MTL-BLSTM-RNN with 1 task-specific layer** (Figure 2a): the 1024-by-2 BLSTM output is *"flattened
  and is connected to the output layer through a fully-connected layer"*, and the five tasks are five
  slices of that one 80-D vector. **There is one task-specific layer for all five tasks.**
- **MTL-BLSTM-RNN with 2 task-specific layers** (Figure 2b): *"the architecture is the same as the
  above, but with an additional task-specific layer before the output layer, in order to further
  increase the model capacity."* Figure 2b draws **five separate fully-connected layers** of
  512 / 512 / 512 / 256 / 128 units, one per task, before the five outputs.

So the five predictions are separate in both, and a per-task sub-network exists only in the second.
**This does not move §S4(a)'s sentence** — five separately predicted labels on one shared encoder is
what the sentence describes and what DP-A's argument is about — but a detail specification quoting
the word *heads* should know that this paper's headline configuration puts one layer between the
shared encoder and all five outputs. Recorded as a precision, **applied nowhere.**

**PRECISION (2) — THE SINGLE-TASK BASELINE EXISTS AND IS MEASURED, AND IT IS THE SEPARATION TAKEN ONE
STEP FURTHER THAN §S4(a) DESCRIBES.** §4, page 93: *"to verify the advantage of MTL, we also consider
the single-task learning (STL) as a baseline approach, where the same BLSTM-RNN is used. As a result,
there are five networks in the STL-BLSTM-RNN model, each for one chord function recognition task
respectively, and are trained individually in the experiment."* **So this paper carries BOTH shapes:
one shared encoder with five heads, and five wholly separate networks** — and it measures them
against each other. That measurement is finding (1) below.

**PRECISION (3) — THE LATER-SYSTEM HALF OF §S4(a)'s SENTENCE IS CORRECT ABOUT THIS PAPER BY
OMISSION.** §S4(a) says *"the later ones add root, bass, tonicised key, harmonic rhythm, pitch-class
set…"*. **This paper predicts no root, no bass, no harmonic rhythm and no pitch-class set** — its
five labels are exactly those in Table 1. Verified at the object rather than inferred from the
sentence.

## ★ The doubt default's own question, ANSWERED — the method IS a candidate for a decision inside L2's charter

**What had to be answered**, as the progress record's carried item (a) states it: *"what the method
DOES and whether it is a candidate for a decision inside L2's charter at all"*, with row 39's
precedent standing for the answer *no*.

**AT THE OBJECT: the answer is YES, and the paper's own title says so.**

The printed title is **"A Variational Autoencoder for Joint Chord and Key Estimation from Audio
Chromagrams"** (page 1, printed 500). The abstract's own first sentence is *"This paper describes a
deep generative approach to jointly estimating chords and keys from music signals."* §I states the
motivation in the terms L2's charter is written in: *"different musical elements are mutually
dependent… the musical key is closely related to the likelihood that a certain chord is played [18],
and chord transitions are more likely to occur on downbeats [23]"*, and the classification model is
*"a deep classification model that jointly estimates chords and keys from chroma vectors"* (§I).

**Against L2's charter sentence, limb by limb** (`FRAMEWORK.md` §5, L2, lines 388–390):

- *"what is the tonality at each moment"* — **YES**, a key label per frame, 24 classes (major and
  minor keys only).
- *"where does each harmony give way to the next"* — **NO decision of its own.** There is no
  boundary variable, no segment-length term and no segmentation output. Temporal continuity is
  imposed AFTER classification by a Viterbi pass with a hand-set self-transition probability (§III-G).
- *"which sounding notes belong to the harmony and which elaborate it"* — **NO**, and it cannot: the
  input is a chroma vector, not notes.
- *"what chord is read over each span"* — **YES**, a chord label per frame, 73 classes.

**So the method answers the tonality limb and the chord limb of L2's one entangled decision, is
silent on the boundary limb, and cannot reach the chord-tone limb at all.** That is the same
tonality-and-chord-without-segmentation shape group 1 holds, reached from the audio side, and it is
a candidate for the coupling boundary condition the L2 charter fixes. **The ADMITTED verdict and the
L2 placement therefore stand CONFIRMED at the object.** **This is not row 39's outcome and must not
be reported as one.**

## What an L2 detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

- **★ ADOPT-OR-ARGUE — A MEASURED INSTANCE OF THE COUPLING BOUNDARY CONDITION IN A THIRD SHAPE THAT
  IS NEITHER A COST NOR A VETO.** The L2 charter fixes that *"the coupling between tonality and chord
  is a cost, never a veto"* (`FRAMEWORK.md` lines 413–420). **This paper's coupling is neither.** Its
  variational posterior states the chord and the key to be conditionally independent given the audio
  (eq. 7), its two Viterbi passes carry separate transition matrices, and **the only place the two
  questions meet is the shared encoder's representation.** So the whole coupling is carried by
  parameter sharing, with **no term in any objective that scores a chord against a key**. **The
  charter's own sentence names two shapes** — *"a soft distance inside a scored path, against a hard
  compatibility constraint"* — **and this is a third**, which the charter's ruling that the coupling
  must be a cost and never a veto does not reach, because there is no coupling term to be either.
  The paper measures what the sharing buys: +2.56 to +3.54 points of key accuracy, −0.47 to +0.38 of chord accuracy,
  and +0.04 to +0.07 of its own consistency measure. Routed to L2's detail specification and to the
  findings surface's DP-B block; **applied nowhere.**
- **★ ADDITION CANDIDATE FOR DP-A's GROUND — A PAPER OF THIS FAMILY THAT MEASURES HEAD DISAGREEMENT
  WITH A PURPOSE-BUILT METRIC, WHICH THE RECORD DOES NOT CARRY.** DP-A's live ground (lines 674–677)
  says *"the papers measure what happens when they are allowed to disagree"*, and §S4(a) says the
  same. **Row 45's finding (1) established that the paper DP-A quotes measures nothing about it**, and
  **row 46 established that its own composite is a conjunction which cannot separate a wrong head
  from heads contradicting each other.** **This paper does measure it**, deliberately and with a
  metric built for the purpose (§IV-A-4, eq. 14), and reports that the joint classifier improves it.
  **This does not correct DP-A** — DP-A's attribution is row 45's open finding and is untouched here —
  **and it does not support DP-A's chosen "no" either**: the measurement runs the other way, showing
  that sharing an encoder REDUCES head disagreement rather than showing that dividing the deciding
  produces it. **It is offered as a ground DP-A's defense could cite and currently does not, with its
  domain and its bounds attached.** Routed to the findings surface's DP-A block and to the user;
  **applied nowhere, and no verdict is proposed.**
- **★ MUST ARGUE AGAINST — SEPARATE PER-FRAME HEADS WITH NO JOINT TERM, THE DIVIDED DECIDING IN ITS
  purest measured form.** The classification model is exactly the shape §S4(a) describes for the
  symbolic lineage — one shared encoder, heads decided in one forward pass, nothing enforcing
  consistency — reached independently in the audio domain and with the two degrees of division
  measured against each other. **What a detail specification arguing DP-A's chosen "no" gets from this
  paper is, as at row 46, evidence about SHARING and not about DIVIDING**: the comparison is a shared
  encoder against two independent networks, and **nothing in the paper measures the cost of splitting
  the answer against not splitting it.** **Rows 46 and 51 both have that structure; that is a
  statement about those two rows and nothing is inferred from it about any other.**
- **★ MUST ARGUE AGAINST — THE FIXED FRAME GRID, HERE AN ACOUSTIC ONE.** Every boundary this model
  can imply is a 46 ms STFT hop, against the L1 charter's change-point grid and the L2 charter's
  *"boundaries are a subset of L1's change points"*. Row 46's grid was a notated subdivision; **this
  one is not derived from the music at all.** The slice already holds the fixed-grid shape at rows 18,
  19, 20, 47 and 46 (each read at its own extract); the rows are named and no count is asserted.
- **★ THE LENGTH-TERM QUESTION: THIS IS ROW 50's SHAPE, REACHED INDEPENDENTLY AND APPLIED TO BOTH
  AXES — NOT A NEW ONE, AND NO NEW COUNT IS ASSERTED.** The progress record's carried item (g) lists
  linear/exponential needing no segmental decode, Gaussian needing it, unbounded-history needing an
  approximate decode, and no length term at all, and records **row 50 as adding a first-order
  self-transition bonus decoded by Viterbi AFTER the labelling on the tonality axis.** **This paper's
  is the same mechanism on BOTH axes** — a hand-set self-transition probability inside a post-hoc
  Viterbi pass, **0.9 for chords and 0.95 for keys**, with no derivation stated for either value and
  no experiment measuring their effect. By row 11's §2.3 test it is the shape a segmental decode does
  no work for; it is applied **after the classifier rather than inside any objective**, so it cannot
  influence what the classifier learns. **What is new here is only that both axes carry it and that
  both values are hand-set and undefended**; row 50's own cost was declared negligible with no figure,
  and this paper publishes no figure for its two values either. Routed to L2's detail specification
  beside D-004; **the rows are named and no count is asserted.**
- **A DATUM ON THE LABEL SPACE, BESIDE THE CANDIDATE-ADMISSION BOUNDARY CONDITION.** The chord
  vocabulary carries an explicit **non-chord label**, beside row 18's `X`, row 47's *'others'* and
  *'no-chord'* and row 46's *'other'*; **the rows are named and no count is asserted.**
  **And the key vocabulary is closed to major and minor by discarding the corpus's other songs**,
  which is an admission rule applied to the DATA rather than to the search — the mirror of the
  question the L2 charter reserves to its own specification. Routed to L2's detail specification.
- **A DATUM FOR MEASUREMENT DESIGN — A PUBLISHED CROSS-HEAD CONSISTENCY METRIC WITH ITS OWN STATED
  ASSUMPTION.** Overlap ∈ {0,1,2,3}, defined only because the chord is a triad, and grounded on *"the
  simple assumption that a chord is more likely to occur when it shares more notes with the current
  key"*. **It cannot separate a chord that is wrong from a chord that is right and chromatic**, and
  the paper does not claim it can. Routed to measurement design as a shape, with that bound attached.
- **A DATUM ON THE TRAINING-DATA PROVENANCE.** The chroma extractor the whole system depends on was
  trained on **synthesised audio from MIDI** (Slakh2100), and is then applied to real recordings.
  Recorded as printed; nothing is carried from it.

## ★ Findings, routed and not applied

**(1) ★ THE DOUBT DEFAULT'S QUESTION IS ANSWERED AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE ROW BELONGS WHERE IT
SITS.** The method decides tonality and chord together over a music signal — the first and last limbs
of L2's charter sentence — so it is a candidate for a decision inside L2's charter and the ADMITTED
verdict and the L2 placement stand **confirmed at the object** rather than merely left standing.
**This is not row 39's outcome.** Two precisions travel with it, and both are about the record's
reasons rather than about its verdicts: the candidacy row's *"nothing in the record settles what its
method does"* is **exactly right** — the sweeps establish that `FRAMEWORK.md`, `population.md` and the
findings surface name it nowhere — and the slice derivation's *"the lineage section places the whole
lineage as DP-A evidence"* is **a placement this paper turns out to fit for a different reason than
the lineage's other members**: it is not a Roman-numeral analyser and predicts no degree, quality or
inversion, so **§S4(a)'s universal does not reach it and nothing here bears on that sentence in
either direction.** Routed to the user; **nothing is amended.**

**(2) ★ AN ADDITION CANDIDATE FOR DP-A's GROUND, STATED AS A CANDIDATE AND NOT AS A CORRECTION.**
The record claims twice — DP-A's live text at lines 674–677 and §S4(a) at lines 1557–1562 — that the
multi-task papers *"measure what happens when they are allowed to disagree"*. Row 45's read
established that the paper DP-A quotes for it measures nothing of the kind; row 46's established that
the lineage's founding paper measures a conjunction, which cannot separate a wrong head from
disagreeing heads. **This paper measures head agreement directly, with a metric proposed for that
purpose, and reports that joint estimation improves it.** **What it does NOT do is support DP-A's
chosen "no"**: the improvement is the joint model's, so the measurement is evidence that a shared
representation reduces disagreement, not evidence that dividing the deciding causes it. **Recorded
BESIDE row 45's finding (1) and row 46's finding, and MERGED WITH NEITHER.** Routed to the findings
surface's DP-A block and to the user; **applied nowhere, and no verdict is proposed.**

**(3) A SECOND AUDIO MEASUREMENT OF THE COST OF SEPARATING TONALITY FROM CHORD, WITH A DIFFERENT SIGN
ON THE CHORD AXIS.** DP-B's recorded ground and §4.2's *"Chord ↔ tonality"* bullet both rest on one
measurement — *"about 2 points of chord accuracy and about 5 points of tonality accuracy over 174
pieces"*, which row 27's read verified at its own object as 1.8 and 4.6. **This paper is a second
audio study of the same comparison**, on 222 songs, and it measures **+2.56 to +3.54 points of key
accuracy and −0.47 to +0.38 points of chord accuracy** for joint over separate. **The tonality side
agrees in direction and is smaller; the chord side does not reproduce — in the supervised pair it runs
the other way.** **No contradiction is asserted between the two studies**: they differ in corpus, in
input representation, in chord vocabulary and in what "joint" means — Rocher's coupling is a term in a
scored path, this one's is parameter sharing with no coupling term at all — **and that difference is
itself the point, because it is the charter's own boundary condition being varied.** Routed to the
findings surface's DP-B block and to L2's detail specification, **recorded beside DP-B's existing
ground and merged with it nowhere**; applied nowhere.

**(4) A PUBLISHED INSTANCE OF SEMI-SUPERVISED TRAINING HELPING ONE AXIS AND HURTING THE OTHER, WITH
THE AUTHORS' OWN MECHANISM.** Adding 350 unannotated songs moved chord accuracy up (+0.59 multi-task,
+0.21 single-task, against the supervised VAE rows) and key accuracy down (−2.05 and −2.40), with the
authors' stated reason that the generative model *"became more vulnerable to the ambiguity in chroma
vectors with respect to key classes"*. Derived with the sign convention stated; read as a direction
only, no uncertainty being printed. **A datum for L2's fitting question (DP-P) and for measurement
design**, beside D-525's staged fit and rows 10's, 11's and 19's fitting findings; routed, applied
nowhere.

**(5) THE AUTHORS' OWN SUMMARY SENTENCE IS NOT BORNE OUT BY THEIR OWN TABLE IN ONE OF THREE PAIRS**
(the relative-key-error claim, derived above), and **one paragraph describes a fall in chord accuracy
as "little improvement"**. Recorded as bounds on what those sentences can be cited for, in the shape
row 49's read used; nothing is carried from either sentence beyond what the table supports.

**(6) A NUMERIC COINCIDENCE RECORDED SO NOBODY MERGES THE TWO.** *"77.03"* is this paper's Table I
Key-correct cell for the multi-task semi-supervised VAE model, and it is also **this project's own
ratified root-agreement baseline** at `CLAUDE.md` lines 817 and 1077. **Two different quantities in
two different documents.** *(The same shape as the row 46 read's "66.65"; recorded for the same
reason and merged with it nowhere.)*

**(7) ★ A SECOND AUTHOR GROUP REPEATS THE CHARACTERISATION OF THE HARMONY TRANSFORMER THAT ROW 47's
READ CORRECTED AT THE OBJECT.** §II, page 2, states: *"The recently proposed harmony transformer [5]
jointly estimates chord sequence and chord transition positions."* Reference [5] is *T. Chen and L.
Su, "Harmony transformer: Incorporating chord segmentation into harmony recognition", ISMIR 2019* —
**candidacy row 47's first paper, read whole at the object by the eleventh session**, whose extract
records that **the training is joint and the deciding is sequential**: the chord-change decision is
committed by a hard threshold at 0.5 and the label decision is then taken conditioned on it. **So a
second, independent author group describes that system the way row 47's read established the system
itself does not work.** **Nothing is carried from this sentence about the Harmony Transformer** — row
47's own object read governs — and **row 47's finding (1) is not restated as settled, applied or
built on here.** Recorded as a datum about how that system is described in the literature, routed to
the findings surface's DP-C block; **applied nowhere.**

**(8) TWO FURTHER DATA FROM §II's RELATED WORK, EACH RECORDED AS PRINTED AND NEITHER FETCHED.**
*(a)* *"A DNN classifier proposed by Mcfee and Bello [22] jointly estimates root notes, bass notes,
and chord tones as well as chord classes"* — **a multi-task chord model carrying a CHORD-TONE head,
in the audio domain**, which is DP-D's excluded rival's shape in a multi-task setting; reference [22]
is *McFee & Bello, "Structured training for large-vocabulary chord recognition", ISMIR 2017*, **which
the bibliography does not hold and for which `reading_pass/extracts/` holds no extract**, both
checked at their own listings this session. *(b)* *"joint estimation of keys and chords is shown to
be beneficial for some musical analysis tasks like music segmentation with proper probabilistic
formulation [25]"* — reference [25] is *Pauwels & Peeters, "Segmenting music through the joint
estimation of keys, chords and structural boundaries", ACM MM 2013, pp. 741–744*, **a published
method that decides tonality, chord AND structural boundary together — all three limbs of L2's
charter sentence that this paper's own method does not reach — and it is neither held nor in the
bibliography**, checked at both objects. **Nothing is carried out of either work**; both are routed
to the bibliography reconciliation and to L2's detail specification as named-but-unread candidates.

**(9) AN INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IN THE PAPER'S OWN CITATION OF ITS CHROMA EXTRACTOR, RECORDED AS
PRINTED AND RECONCILED NOWHERE.** §III-A (page 2) says the chroma vectors *"are extracted from the
music signal using a pre-trained DNN chroma extractor proposed in [28]"*, where [28] is *Wu & Li,
"Automatic audio chord recognition with MIDI-trained deep feature and BLSTM-CRF sequence decoding
model", IEEE TASLP 27(2):355–366, 2019*. §IV-A-3 (page 5) says *"The DNN-based chroma extractor [29]
used for obtaining **X** was trained with Slakh2100 dataset [20]"*, where [29] is *Wu, Carsault,
Nakamura & Yoshii, arXiv:2005.07091, 2020*. **The paper names two different references for the one
component every figure in it depends on.** Recorded as printed; **the paper reconciles them nowhere
and neither does this extract.** A datum for measurement design about provenance of a load-bearing
front end.

**(10) THE BIBLIOGRAPHY ROW CARRIES NO TITLE, SO A TITLE MATCH IS IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION.** The
printed title is recorded above as a fact about the held file; authors, venue, year and pagination all
match, and the printed copyright line carries **no CC licence**, so the row's LINK tier is correct.

## Centrality — NOT CENTRAL, and the ground on which CENTRAL could be argued is stated in full

**NOT CENTRAL.** **No ratified text names this paper, no `[FACT]` rests on it, no figure of it is
reported anywhere in the staged tree, and `population.md`'s thirteen verification rows do not name
it** — all four established at the objects by the sweeps and the whole reading recorded in the banner,
not inherited. Nothing in a BLSTM-over-chroma variational autoencoder would be adopted: the input is
audio, the grid is acoustic, the label space is 73 triads and 24 major/minor keys, and the method
decides no segmentation, no degree, no inversion, no bass and no chord-tone assignment. Every figure
is a single run with no uncertainty of any kind and no significance test.

**The ground on which CENTRAL could be argued, stated in full so the verdict is challengeable
here:** the paper **measures cross-head consistency with a metric built for it**, which is the exact
quantity DP-A's live ground claims the multi-task papers measure and which **rows 45's and 46's reads
established their own papers do not**; a detail specification defending DP-A's chosen "no" would have
to meet it, if only to say that its measurement runs the other way. **Whether any other read row of
this slice carries such a metric is NOT established here** — that would need those rows' own extracts
read, which this session did not do — **so this is a statement about rows 45, 46 and 51 and about no
others.** It is also an instance of a tonality-and-chord coupling carried entirely by parameter
sharing, which is a shape the L2 charter's coupling sentence does not contemplate. **A reader who
takes either of those as load-bearing should read the verdict as CENTRAL and the second extraction as
OWED; the choice is recorded here so it can be made.**

**A SECOND INDEPENDENT EXTRACTION IS THEREFORE NOT OWED** by this verdict, and the verdict is
challengeable at the progress record.

**At the object, §6 (page 5):** *"A major problem in applying the MMI criterion is the fact that the
reference translations need to be part of the provided n-best list. Quite often, none of the given
reference translations is part of the n-best list because the search algorithm performs pruning …

n-best list all the sentences which have a minimal number of word errors with respect to any of the
true references. Note that due to this selection approach, the results of the MMI criterion might
be biased toward the mWER criterion. It is a major advantage of the minimum error rate training
that it is not necessary to choose pseudo-references."* `[FACT — quoted at the object.]`

**And §7 (page 6) says it a second time, with the authors' own expectation attached:** *"The MMI
criterion produces significantly worse results on all error rates besides mWER. Note that, due to the
re-definition of the notion of reference translation by using minimum edit distance, the results of
the MMI criterion are biased toward mWER. It can be expected that by using a suitably defined
n-gram precision to define the pseudo-references for MMI instead of using edit distance, it is
possible to obtain better BLEU or NIST scores."* `[FACT — quoted at the object.]`

7): *"We showed that this approach obtains significantly better results than using the MMI training

## Finding (7) — the algorithm itself, which is what could be ADOPTED

**At the object, §5 (pages 3–5).** Along a line in parameter space, $\lambda_1^M + \gamma \cdot d_1^M$,
each candidate translation's score is a line in $\gamma$, so the minimum over candidates,
$f(\gamma;\mathbf{f}) = \min_{\mathbf{e}\in\mathbf{C}}\{t(\mathbf{e},\mathbf{f}) + \gamma\cdot
m(\mathbf{e},\mathbf{f})\}$, **is piecewise linear** (the paper credits Papineni 1999). The exhaustive
representation of that function is computed per sentence as an ordered sequence of interval boundaries
with the change in error count at each; merging the sequences over the corpus gives the complete set of
boundaries, and **the optimal $\gamma$ is found by traversing them while updating an error count**.
*"The new algorithm is much faster and more stable than the grid-based line optimization method."* It
extends to BLEU and NIST *"by accumulating the relevant statistics for computing these scores (n-gram
precision, translation length and reference length)"*. `[FACT — read at the object.]`

**What an L2 detail specification could take.** Our own combination weights are a small vector over
factor scores and each candidate reading's score is linear in them, so the same construction applies
directly; and our own hard stop is a corpus-level accumulated count (a duration), which is the shape
the BLEU/NIST extension handles. **This is the concrete content of the candidacy row's *"its METHOD …
is the live candidate for DP-P"*, and it is stated here so a later specification cites the mechanism and
not the headline figure.** **Domain: machine translation. Nothing here was measured on music.**

## Finding (8) — the candidate list is fitted against, and the paper's own remedy is an outer loop

**At the object, §6 (page 5):** *"Using an n-best approximation, we might face the problem that the

resulting n-best list does not change."* *"In our experiments, we compute in every iteration about 200

specification beside the charter's candidate-admission boundary condition and beside **D-098** (the

## What an L2 detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

- **Adopt (the score form, which is the candidacy row's own reason):** equation (1) — a score over candidate
  readings formed as the exponential of a weighted sum of feature functions over the cliques of a fixed
  graph, with the weights fitted and the features given. This is the published form of *"how the score over
  candidate readings is formed, what its terms are, what tables they read, and how any weight is fitted"*
  that the L2 charter (`FRAMEWORK.md` lines 406–408) leaves to the detail specification. **The paper decides
  the FORM and expressly not the TERMS** — the features are given and fixed — so it answers half of the
  charter's sentence and is silent on the other half.
- **Adopt (the normalisation, and its placement):** the observation-dependent partition function Z_θ(x)
  computed as a matrix product over the sequence, with the exact forward–backward recursions of §4 — so that
  a normalised distribution over whole readings, and per-span marginals, are available rather than only a
  best path. Beside **D-006** (two full candidate lists, no truncation), **D-008** (true probabilities
  deferred) and **DP-K** (rivals with their mass); row 11's finding (10) recorded this datum at the
  segmental extension and it is recorded here at the base formalism, the two named and merged nowhere.
- **Adapt (the HMM-like construction as the published route from a counted table to a fitted score):** §3's
  particular case builds a CRF whose features are exactly the state-pair and state-observation indicators of
  an HMM, so that *"the corresponding parameters λ_{y′,y} and μ_{y,x} play a similar role to the (logarithms
  of the) usual HMM parameters"*. That is the shape **D-525**'s staged fit already has read from the other
  side: the counted-and-frozen tables become the model's features, and what is fitted is the vector of
  weights over them. Routed to L2's detail specification beside **D-525** and DP-P as a published precedent
  for the construction, not as a derivation of ours.
- **Adapt (the convexity property, with its qualification, as a design check):** footnote 2 makes the global
  optimum conditional on fully observable states. L2's state carries tonality, boundary, chord-tone
  assignment and chord together; whether every component of it is observed in the ground truth decides
  whether this property is available at all. Routed to L2's detail specification and to measurement design
  as a check to run, not as an answer.
- **Must argue against — the paper's own named rivals, each with the paper's own ground:** the
  generate-candidates-then-rerank pipeline, rejected because *"these methods fail when the correct output is
  pruned away in the first pass"*; locally normalised conditional models, rejected on label bias; local
  gradient-descent methods over per-label losses, rejected because their loss is not convex; and a fully

  figure is on synthetic data or English POS tagging. It carries a FORMAL and a MEASURED-ON-TEXT result and

## What an L2 detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

**ADOPT: nothing.** There is no mechanism here to take.

**ADAPT: one rule, and it is a rule about choosing, not about computing.** *Where the same family of
scores can be fitted either by counting a joint model or by fitting a conditional one
discriminatively, which is better depends on how much annotated material there is relative to the
number of free parameters — and the two orderings cross.* **`D-525`'s staged fit sits exactly on
that axis**: its factor tables are **counted from ground truth and frozen** (the generative side)
and only a **small vector of combination weights is fitted discriminatively** (the discriminative
side), with an all-weights-equal ablation arm that must be beaten. This paper is the published
general account of the axis that decision sits on — **it is not a defence of `D-525` and does not
mention anything like it**, but a specification defending `D-525` against a fully discriminative
rival is arguing on this paper's ground, and rows 10's and 11's fully discriminative fits are the
rival's instances already read in this slice.

**MUST ARGUE AGAINST: Proposition 1.** The paper's first formal result is that the discriminative
member of a pair has the **lower asymptotic error**. A specification that keeps a counted, frozen
generative component is choosing the member with the higher asymptote, and the honest defence is the
sample-complexity one (Lemma 3, Corollary 6) — not a claim that the counted tables are better in the
limit. **The paper forecloses that second defence explicitly.**

**AND MUST ARGUE AGAINST THE TRANSFER ITSELF, WHICH IS THE HARDER HALF.** Every result above is
stated for **iid examples, a fixed feature set, binary labels and two linear classifiers**. L2's
score is a structured object over a decoded sequence of spans with a segmentation variable. **The
paper establishes nothing about that setting**, its own stated extension reaches only a
fixed-structure bounded-fan-in Bayesian network, and **nothing in this extract asserts the transfer
holds.** A specification citing this paper for L2's fitting regime must establish the transfer at
the object or state that it has not.

## ★ Findings, routed and not applied

### (1) ★★ THE DOUBT DEFAULT'S OWN QUESTION IS ANSWERED — YES, IT CARRIES THE INFERENCE AND FITTING DETAIL, BY EXPLANATION AND NOT BY MEASUREMENT

The candidacy row's question is *"whether it carries the inference and fitting detail the three CRF rows
above leave out."* **At the object it does**: §1.3.2 carries the regularised objective, its gradient, the
concavity argument and the optimiser class with its evidence named; §1.3.3 carries the exact recursions
and the per-span marginal; §1.4.3 carries the latent-variable objective with both optimisation routes;
§1.4.4 the approximate-inference options; §1.4.6 the implementation practices. **Rows 12, 11 and 10 leave
exactly that out** — row 12's extract records its paper's two iterative-scaling algorithms and its own
statement that slow convergence is its main limitation; this chapter is where the replacement is
explained and the replacement's evidence is cited, and one of those citations is row 14, already read.

**What it carries, it carries as a SECONDARY SOURCE.** Every load-bearing sentence above cites a primary:
row 12 for the form; Bertsekas 1999 and Byrd et al. 1994 for the optimisers; row 14, Wallach 2002, Malouf
2002 and Minka 2003 for the evidence that they beat iterative scaling; Culotta & McCallum 2004 for the
per-span marginal; Quattoni et al. 2005 and McCallum et al. 2005 for latent-variable CRFs; Yedidia et al.
2004 for loopy belief propagation. **Of those, rows 12 and 14 are held and read; the others are not held.**
The item (d′) case arose exactly as the progress record said it might: **the chapter's one measurement of
its own (§1.5) is not about the detail the row was admitted for**, so the question is answered by what the
chapter EXPLAINS, and this extract says so.

**★ THE ADMITTED VERDICT AND THE L2 PLACEMENT STAND, with a precision to the reason.** The candidacy row
calls it *"a tutorial rather than a primary method"* — true at the object — and the slice derivation
places it *"for the inference and fitting detail rows 10–12 leave out"* — also true at the object. The
precision: **what the detail is, is a secondary account whose primaries are partly held (rows 12 and 14)
and partly not (the seven works named above)**, so a detail specification citing this chapter for any of
it is citing a source that itself cites another, and the theory-grounding corollary's unfetched-source
rule reaches the not-held primaries. **Routed as a precision to the candidacy row's reason and to the
slice derivation's line 63, and as a not-held-primary list to the bibliography reconciliation. Applied
nowhere; both files stand exactly as they stand.**

### (2) THERE IS NO VERIFICATION TARGET — rows 51's, 12's, 13's and 14's shape

Established at the objects by the legs named at the top of this extract. **The record bears on the paper
in exactly three places and `FRAMEWORK.md` is not one of them.** No `[FACT]`, no ratified figure and no
characterisation rests on it; this read corrects nothing, confirms no ratified value, and had no recorded
structural claim to correct.

### (3) ★ ROW 15's "MMI" AND ROW 12's "CONDITIONAL LIKELIHOOD" ARE ONE CRITERION, AND THIS CHAPTER SAYS SO IN TERMS — A PRECISION FOR HOW DP-P's SENTENCE IS READ

`FRAMEWORK.md` DP-P and §S6's DP16 say *"fitting combination weights by likelihood"*. Row 15's extract
records that the arm behind that phrase is Och's **MMI** criterion, which it calls *"the likelihood-type
criterion"* and which Och derives from the maximum-entropy principle. Row 12's extract records the CRF's
fit as the **conditional log-likelihood**. **This chapter joins them at p. 22:** training a directed model
by conditional likelihood *"is commonly done in the speech community, where it is called maximum mutual
information training"*, and it *"is no easier"* than in a CRF because log p(x) *"plays the same role as
Z(x)"*. **So the likelihood arm Och measured at 12.2 against 19.6 and the fit rows 12 and 10 use are the
same criterion by this chapter's own identification**, and the two halves of DP-P's question — the
criterion, and what fitting to the metric instead buys — are now read at three primaries and one
secondary that names the identity. **A precision on the reading of a recorded sentence, not a correction:
nothing the record says is false.** Routed to L2's detail specification and to the findings surface's DP-P
block, beside row 15's three precisions and row 13's finding (4) and merged with none of them. **Applied
nowhere.**

### (4) ★ THE LATENT-VARIABLE REGIME IS THE OTHER SIDE OF ROW 12's CONVEXITY QUALIFICATION, AND IT IS THE CHECK THAT DECIDES WHICH FITTING REGIME L2 IS EVEN IN

Row 12's extract routed *"the convexity property, with its qualification, as a design check"*: the global
optimum holds *"in the case of fully observable states"*, and *"whether every component of [L2's state] is
observed in the ground truth decides whether this property is available at all."* **This chapter supplies
what that check leads to on its other branch.** If any component of L2's state — the L2 charter publishes the
segmentation, and per span the tonality and the chord, and per sounding note the chord-tone assignment
and, where the reading has one, the elaboration relation (`FRAMEWORK.md` 392–398) — is NOT observed in
the ground truth the weights are fitted on, then the fit is a latent-variable CRF: the objective is the
marginal likelihood (1.45), *"no longer convex in general"*, reached only to a local maximum that depends on
initialisation, by direct gradient (1.52) or EM (1.53), with no published comparison of the two as of the
chapter. **Whether any such component is unobserved in this project's ground truth is NOT established here
and nothing in this extract asserts it either way** — it is a question about what the annotation records,
which is answered at the ground truth and at `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s statement of what the tables are counted
from, neither of which this read opened. **Routed to L2's detail specification and to measurement design
as the question that must be answered before the fitting regime is written down, beside D-525 (the staged
fit), D-271 (the capacity budget), DP-P and row 12's routed check. Applied nowhere; no verdict.**

### (5) THE PER-SPAN MARGINAL IS A PUBLISHED ROUTE TO A CONFIDENCE OVER A STRETCH, AND ITS PRIMARY IS NOT HELD

Page 15 names constrained forward-backward (Culotta & McCallum 2004) as the way to compute
p(y_t … y_{t+k} | x) over a range of nodes, *"for measuring the model's confidence in its predicted
labeling over a segment of input."* **D-006** publishes two full candidate lists, **D-008** defers true
probabilities, **D-032** requires every confidence to be class-declared and named to its decision, and
DP-K publishes rivals with their mass. **This is a published construction for a per-span probability
inside the same normalised model, and the record does not name it.** An ADDITION CANDIDATE for the design
data under those decisions, carried with its bound: **the primary is not held, and this chapter states the
construction's existence and use, not its algorithm.** Routed to L2's detail specification. **Shown, not
ratified.**

### (6) THE TRAINING-COST STATEMENT, AND WHAT IT IS A DATUM FOR

O(TM²NG) with two worked cases, and the stated main disadvantage at §1.6. **M here is the number of
states of the chain** — for L2, the size of the joint state space over tonality, chord and whatever else
the state carries — and the cost is quadratic in it per position. A datum beside `CLAUDE.md`'s standing
rule that getting the inference right comes first and speed is traded against it only once slowness has
turned out to be a problem — **the rule sequences the concern and does not license ignoring it** — and
beside row 12's finding (13), which recorded the same limitation from the primary. **This chapter dates it
and gives it a formula; it measures nothing of ours.** Routed as a datum. **No verdict.**

### (7) THE RIVAL OBJECTIVES ARE ENUMERATED, AND THE ABSENCE OF A CAREFUL COMPARISON IS STATED — DATED TO THE CHAPTER

§1.4.5's list — generative likelihood, conditional likelihood, pseudolikelihood, max-margin, averaged
perceptron — is the set DP-P's question chooses among, and the chapter's *"little careful comparison of
these … across different structures and domains"* is a FACT of absence **as of this chapter's writing,
bounded by its reference list at late 2005, and not a statement about the field now.** Routed to L2's
detail specification and to measurement design as the enumeration a specification must at least name.
**No verdict.**

### (8) THE DOMAIN CROSSING, STATED ONCE AND BINDING ON EVERY CLAIM ABOVE

The chapter's subject is machine learning on text: named-entity recognition and part-of-speech tagging as
running examples, and information extraction from 485 seminar announcements as its one experiment.
**There is nothing musical anywhere in the thirty-five pages.** Row 11's extract, read at its own line 379
this session, writes the bound: *"so the formalism paper is not later cited as if it measured the musical
gain"*. **The same bound binds here: nothing in this chapter measures anything about harmony, and no
figure of it may be cited as evidence about this project's repertoire, its corpus or its accuracy.**

### (9) THE ORDINARY DATA, RECORDED AS PRINTED

- **No uncertainty of any kind on any figure, and no significance test anywhere** (§1.5 above).
- **The cross-primary check RAN ON SOMETHING, and what it found is consistency and not a figure.** This
  chapter cites four held members of the population — rows 12, 11, 13 and 14 — and what it says of each
  agrees with that row's own extract read this session: row 12's iterative scaling as the superseded
  training approach (row 12's own §7 limitation); row 14's 3.8 million features and its matching of
  state-of-the-art noun-phrase chunking (row 14's extract at its lines 118 and 133, read this session);
  row 13's generative–discriminative pair (row 13's extract's §1 quotation); row 11's semi-Markov CRF
  described by its feature flexibility only. **No figure of any of them is reported here, so nothing is
  merged.**
- **★ THE REFERENCE LIST: fifty-nine works, derived at the pages, of which FOUR are in this project's
  bibliography and have extracts — rows 12, 11, 13 and 14 — and fifty-five are not held and have none.**
  The not-held members this extract's findings lean on are named at finding (1). **Nothing is carried out
  of any of them.** *(Rows 15's, 12's and 13's outcome — no member held — does NOT recur here; the rows are
  named and no comparison beyond that is asserted.)*
- **No datum for DP-O, DP-N or any other underived design point** — the chapter's only sentence toward a
  grammar is the §1.4.2 remark that CRFs have been used *"to learn distributions over the derivations of
  a grammar"*, a citation list and nothing more.
- **No printing inconsistency was found.** Every section, equation, figure and table number the text
  refers to exists as printed. *(Rows 12's and 52's shape did not recur.)*

## Centrality

**NOT CENTRAL, and the ground on which CENTRAL could be argued is stated in full so the verdict is
challengeable.**

**The ground for NOT CENTRAL, in four parts.**
1. **The load-bearing-claim route is absent and was established, not assumed.** No `[FACT]`, no ratified
   figure and no characterisation rests on this paper — the legs at the top of this extract. **This is
   rows 51's, 12's, 13's and 14's situation; rows 51 and 13 were graded NOT CENTRAL and rows 12 and 14
   CENTRAL, so this part decides nothing alone.**
2. **It is a SECONDARY source, and every claim a specification would cite it for has a primary.** Row 12
   was graded CENTRAL because its formalism IS the family L2's score would instantiate; this chapter
   restates that formalism from the HMM side and adds the machinery around it — and for each piece of
   machinery it names the primary. Under #1 and the theory-grounding corollary a detail specification
   cites the primary it has read, or states the gap; **it does not cite the tutorial in the primary's
   place.** Where the primary is held (rows 12 and 14), the tutorial adds nothing a specification would
   cite; where it is not (Culotta & McCallum 2004, Quattoni et al. 2005, McCallum et al. 2005, the three
   optimiser demonstrations), the tutorial is what a specification would cite ONLY with the gap stated,
   which is part 4's point.
3. **Nothing of its own would be adopted.** Its one design — skip edges between identical capitalised
   words — is about repeated proper names in text, and its one measurement is that design's F1 on one
   information-extraction data set, with no uncertainty printed.
4. **The domain.** Nothing musical anywhere; every figure is text-processing.

**The ground on which CENTRAL could be argued, stated so the user or a later session can overrule this
verdict.** Findings (3), (4) and (5) are claims an L2 detail specification would have to make — the
identity of the likelihood arms, the latent-variable regime if the state is partly unobserved, and the
per-span marginal as a confidence route — **and for (4) and (5) this chapter is a HELD source that states
them where their primaries are not held; whether any OTHER held paper states either was NOT checked, and
no superlative is asserted.** If the user reads either as load-bearing for the specification, the commission's second
route is satisfied and the verdict flips; the reason this side did not take that route is part 2 above —
**the chapter would then be cited for a claim whose primary was not read, which the corollary permits only
as a stated gap, and a source citable only as a stated gap is not central by that fact.** **The judgment is
stated so it can be overruled.**

**Second independent extraction: NOT OWED**, on this verdict. **It flips to owed if the user reads finding
(4) or (5) as load-bearing** — stated here so the choice is his, rows 47's, 51's and 13's treatment.

## Cross-primary check against row 18 (mandatory item (j)) — NOT COMPARABLE, and why

The paper says its HMM-MD is *"the same as in [13]"* and that its best rates are *"a more than twofold
improvement over theirs using the same training set and evaluation script."* Row 18's extract, on disk,
transcribes Sheh & Ellis's Table 3: recognition frame accuracy for their best system (PCP_ROT, train18) is
**23.3** on "Eight Days a Week" and **20.1** on "Every Little Thing"; with the test songs in training
(train20) the base PCP system reaches 23.6 and 26.4. *Derived here:* this paper's best HMM-MD cell, 48.8,
is 2.09 times 23.3 and 1.85 times 26.4 — so *"more than twofold"* holds against the figure the record
carries (23.3) and not against every cell of row 18's table.

**The two are NOT COMPARABLE as measurements, on four grounds established at the two objects:** (1) the
protocol — row 18 tests two hand-marked songs against eighteen training songs, this paper tests every song
once under ten folds; (2) the label set — row 18's 147 defined labels with sevenths, this paper's 48
triads; (3) the feature — row 18's 24-dimensional PCP, this paper's 12-dimensional; (4) the front end —
row 18's 100 ms step, this paper's 92 ms hop with no tuning adjustment. **And this paper runs NO
forced-alignment condition, so it does not bear on the 68.8/23.3 pair DP-C's ground carries, in either
direction.** Recorded as NOT COMPARABLE rather than merged, as rows 46's, 51's, 15's, 12's and 13's reads
had to.
